title: eludite.debug.restart input
description: Debug > Restart (Ctrl+Shift+F5): end the debugging session and start it again with the same configuration. With an adapter that has DAP's `restart` request (`capabilities.restart`) the adapter restarts the debuggee in the same session; otherwise Eludite stops it (as Shift+F5) and starts the same project, launch profile and debug flag again, building first when the setting build.beforeRun says so. Breakpoints, watches and exception settings carry over. Refused when no session runs (mode `design`) and for an attached session (Visual Studio disables Restart there too: detach with eludite.debug.stop and attach again). The answer is the stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json), given as soon as the new session's program runs (`mode: running`), as eludite.debug.start's: a break or the end is answered only when it came before the program was seen running. Set the breakpoints you need first (eludite.debug.toggle_breakpoint with `remove_after`), then call eludite.debug.wait with `until: stopped` for the first stop or the end. A multi-targeted project runs the framework `ActiveDebugFramework` in its `.user` file selects, when it lists it, else its first, as eludite.debug.start does.
x-eludite-escalates: Dangerous when the solution's policy sets `debug.drive` to `prompt`; refused for agents when it sets `debug.drive` to `deny`.

session.description: The debugging session to act on (brief 0028): its `id`, from eludite.debug.sessions or `sessions` in eludite.debug.state. Default: the active session, the one the Locals, Watch, Call Stack and Threads windows show and the execution point follows. An unknown or ended id is refused with the ids of the live sessions.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the new session's program to run (or to break or end before it is seen running) before answering, in milliseconds. From the UI the command never waits; from another thread (an agent) the default is 5000. A build before the launch counts against it. After a `running` answer, call eludite.debug.wait (`until: stopped`) for the first stop.

depth.description: How many levels of the locals to expand: 1 (default) lists the top level only; up to 5. Expansion is breadth-first and stops when `max_variables` rows are listed.

max_variables.description: The most variable rows listed, counting every level (default 50, at most 500).

max_value_chars.description: Values longer than this are cut and end with `… (N chars)`, the row saying `value_truncated` (default 200, at most 10000).

max_frames.description: The most stack frames listed (default 10, at most 200); page further with eludite.debug.stack.

max_output_lines.description: The most program output lines listed (default 20, at most 1000; 0 lists none).

output_since.description: An output cursor (`output.next` of an earlier answer, or eludite.debug.output's `next`): list the program's lines from it on. Default: the last `max_output_lines` lines.
